species.note: Resident on rocky edges year round. The bread-and-butter fish here; holds tight to structure and comes back to the same rock.
Schools more than sargus and less spooky. Often the first fish on a new mark, which makes it a decent test of whether a mark is real.
Lives in holes, caves and under overhangs — the highest relief affinity in this list. Protected or restricted in parts of the Adriatic; CHECK THE CURRENT RULES before targeting it.

Roaming predator that works drop-off edges rather than sitting on structure. Needs clear water and long, still waits. Rare in the shallow north Adriatic shelf — expect this one to score low here most days, and treat a high score as worth the drive.
Works soft bottom and seagrass, not rock — so it scores where the rest of the model scores low. Extremely wary in clear water; coloured water is your friend.
The exception to everything else in this file. Hunts stirred, coloured water and river outflow — the conditions that make the day look bad. Best on the days you would otherwise stay home.
Rubble and rock edges, in holes. Barely cares about visibility and does not spook, so it salvages otherwise poor days. Best in the cooler months.
Seagrass and sand, strongly seasonal — the spring inshore spawning run is the window. Scores where rock-loving species do not.
